typical_summer.rank_note: the median of 1011 summer days with a PHL high of 78-88°F

heat.label: Heatwave
heat.history: July 1993 Philadelphia heat wave (100+ heat deaths) led to the city's Heat Health Emergency program and Heatline.

moderate.label: Typical — Jul 19, 2020
moderate.note: the median of 206 hot days (PHL high ≥ 92°F) since 2010

severe.label: Severe — Jul 20, 2019
severe.note: the 12th-worst of 206 hot days (PHL high ≥ 92°F) since 2010

extreme.label: Record — Jul 22, 2011
extreme.note: the worst of 206 hot days (PHL high ≥ 92°F) since 2010

refuge.label: Open cooling sites
refuge.desc: The city's 28 designated cooling sites (libraries, PHA and rec centers, community partners) open at their posted hours.

transit.label: Free SEPTA to cooling
transit.desc: Cooling sites open, plus free fares to the nearest one, so more people are willing to make the trip.

alert.label: Early heat alert
alert.desc: Heat Health Emergency declared a day early: Heatline, block-captain checks, outdoor work shifted to dawn.

smoke.label: Wildfire smoke
smoke.history: June 2023 Canadian wildfire smoke pushed Philadelphia's AQI into the hazardous range and triggered a Code Red.

moderate.label: Typical — May 31, 2023
moderate.note: the median of 22 smoke days since 2010 (AQI ≥ 101 under a satellite-mapped smoke plume)

severe.label: Severe — Jun 6, 2023
severe.note: the 3rd-worst of 22 smoke days since 2010 (AQI ≥ 101 under a satellite-mapped smoke plume)

extreme.label: Record — Jun 7, 2023
extreme.note: the worst of 22 smoke days since 2010 (AQI ≥ 101 under a satellite-mapped smoke plume)

refuge.label: Clean-air rooms
refuge.desc: The city's 28 cooling sites run as HEPA-filtered clean-air rooms at their posted hours.

n95.label: N95 giveaway
n95.desc: Free N95s at libraries, rec centers and outreach vans; masks cut outdoor PM2.5 dose ~70%.

alert.label: Code Red air alert
alert.desc: Early air-quality alert: outdoor events cancelled, outdoor work paused above AQI 200.

flood.label: Flash flood
flood.unit: in of rain in past 3 h
flood.history: The record day (July 28, 2013) is PHL's heaviest 3-hour rainfall since 2010. Ida (Sept 2021) flooded the Schuylkill and I-676 mostly from upstream rain, which this rainfall-only model does not capture.

moderate.label: Typical — Aug 27, 2011
moderate.note: the median of 59 downpours (≥ 1 in of rain in 3 h at PHL) since 2010

severe.label: Severe — Sep 16, 2017
severe.note: the 4th-worst of 59 downpours (≥ 1 in of rain in 3 h at PHL) since 2010

extreme.label: Record — Jul 28, 2013
extreme.note: the worst of 59 downpours (≥ 1 in of rain in 3 h at PHL) since 2010

refuge.label: Emergency shelters
refuge.desc: City sites outside the FEMA flood zone open as shelters from 3pm; flood-zone residents told to evacuate.

closures.label: Pre-emptive road closures
closures.desc: Flood-prone roads (Kelly/MLK Dr, I-676, riverside) closed before the storm; trips rerouted.

alert.label: Early flood warning
alert.desc: Flash-flood warning pushed 3 hours earlier with 'don't drive' guidance.

cold.label: Winter storm
cold.history: Philadelphia Code Blue: declared when temperature or wind chill drops to 20°F or below; unsheltered residents at highest risk.

moderate.label: Typical — Jan 27, 2022
moderate.note: the median of 440 Code Blue days (wind chill ≤ 20°F) since 2010

severe.label: Severe — Jan 2, 2018
severe.note: the 23rd-worst of 440 Code Blue days (wind chill ≤ 20°F) since 2010

extreme.label: Record — Jan 7, 2014
extreme.note: the worst of 440 Code Blue days (wind chill ≤ 20°F) since 2010

refuge.label: Open warming sites
refuge.desc: The city's 31 Code Blue warming sites open at their posted hours.

outreach.label: Outreach to 24-hour sites
outreach.desc: Homeless outreach vans bring unsheltered residents to the nearest 24-hour warming site.

alert.label: Early Code Blue
alert.desc: Code Blue declared early with utility shutoff moratorium; heat restored for many shut-off homes.

reasons.unaware: didn't hear the warning, kept their routine
reasons.avoid_hazard: heard the warning and stayed in instead of going out
reasons.shift_early: moved the activity to a safer hour of the day
reasons.work_continues: employer kept the outdoor shift going
reasons.alert_shift: employer shifted or paused outdoor work after the official alert
reasons.self_break: took an indoor break from outdoor work
reasons.seek_refuge: went to the official refuge (cooling / clean-air / warming center or shelter)
reasons.too_far: refuge was too far to reach without a car or transit
reasons.informal_refuge: spent hours in a nearby library or rec centre to escape conditions
reasons.no_option: had nowhere better to go, stayed put
reasons.ac_cost: has AC but kept it off to save on the electric bill
reasons.evacuate: left a flood-prone home for the shelter
reasons.delay_trip: waited out the storm before driving
reasons.detour: road closure forced a detour around flooded streets
reasons.heat_restored: utility shutoff moratorium restored their heat
reasons.masked: wore an N95 from the giveaway
